name: Nose
blurb: The top of the ship: the escape tower, the cover, the crew capsule, its heat shield and everything the crew needs.

rows.name: Escape tower
rows.role: A solid rocket on top that pulls the capsule clear of a failing booster.

rows.name: Nose cover / fairing
rows.role: What sits on the capsule's nose: a fairing, a cover or a nose cap.

rows.name: Heat shield
rows.role: Protects the capsule when it falls back through the air.

rows.name: Trunk, adapter & kick stage
rows.role: What joins the capsule to the stage below, and an optional final solid motor.

rows.name: Abort engines
rows.role: Engines in the capsule wall that push it clear: an escape with no tower.

rows.name: Parachutes & floats
rows.role: Slowing down for the landing and staying afloat after splashdown.

rows.name: Air, water, cooling & shelter
rows.role: Keeping the crew alive between the planets.

rows.name: Steering in space
rows.role: Pointing the ship where there is no air.

shapes.name: Small capsule under an escape tower
shapes.desc: One seat under a red truss tower. The tower's motor yanks the capsule clear if the booster fails, and is thrown away on a good flight.
pros: Escape tower: up to +2 % ship reliability (the whole-ship bonus is capped at 6 %)
cons: One cramped seat and only 300 W of power
Small heat shield: 45 m² of entry drag against 80 for the medium one, so the engines brake harder at Mars

shapes.name: Capsule with a recovery nose
shapes.desc: No fairing and no tower: the capsule's own narrow nose holds the main parachute and a rendezvous radar. Gemini crews relied on ejection seats (pick them inside the cabin). The real Gemini cabin was black; the Mk2 here is white.
cons: No escape tower
Blunt nose: more drag

shapes.name: Command module under tower and cover
shapes.real: Apollo on Saturn IB and Saturn V (1968–75)
shapes.desc: A big blunt cabin with the escape tower standing on its nose. On Apollo a cork-and-fibreglass cover wrapped the whole cabin during the climb; the game draws only its top collar. Three main chutes and two drogues bring it home.
pros: Escape tower: up to +3 % ship reliability (the whole-ship bonus is capped at 6 %)
Lands safely on two of three mains
cons: Heavy: needs a large extra tank and a pair of solid boosters (about $4.8M in all on the Reliable body)
Tall nose: needs engine steering (a gimbal ring) or bigger fins

shapes.name: Capsule under a fairing with an escape tower
shapes.real: Soyuz (since 1967); Shenzhou is built the same way
shapes.desc: The escape tower stands on the fairing, and in an abort the whole front end flies away with the crew. Four grid fins fold out to keep it straight.
pros: The escape system that saved Soyuz T-10a
Up to +3 % ship reliability (the whole-ship bonus is capped at 6 %)
cons: Heavy: needs one more tank and a pair of solid boosters
Tall nose: needs engine steering (a gimbal ring) or bigger fins

shapes.name: Big cabin under an abort tower
shapes.desc: A large cabin with its own spare oxygen under the strongest escape system built. Three main chutes, two drogues.
pros: Abort tower: up to +3.5 % ship reliability (the whole-ship bonus is capped at 6 %)
cons: The heaviest nose: needs a large extra tank and a pair of solid boosters (about $4.9M in all on the Reliable body)
Tall nose: needs engine steering (a gimbal ring) or bigger fins
The most expensive nose

shapes.name: Capsule with pusher abort engines and a trunk
shapes.desc: No tower: four pods of engines in the capsule wall push it clear. A hinged cap covers the docking port, and a trunk with solar cells rides underneath.
pros: Abort pods: up to +2.5 % ship reliability (the whole-ship bonus is capped at 6 %)
cons: Heavy: needs one more tank and a pair of solid boosters
Tall nose: needs engine steering (a gimbal ring) or bigger fins
Toxic hypergolic propellant

shapes.name: Capsule under a pointed fairing
shapes.real: Vostok on the R-7: the cabin rode inside a shroud, with no escape tower
shapes.desc: A sharp shroud that encloses the capsule: low drag through the thick air, but no escape tower (Vostok's cosmonaut had an ejection seat). Vostok's cabin was a 2.3 m sphere; here the shroud covers your capsule.
cons: No escape tower
Tall nose: may need bigger fins
The fairing is mass you carry to Mars

shapes.name: Bare capsule
shapes.real: A capsule flown as its own nose, the cheapest crew nose
shapes.desc: The capsule itself is the nose: no fairing, no tower, no trunk.
cons: More drag on the way up
No escape system

shapes.name: Payload stack with a kick motor
shapes.desc: A fairing over the capsule, which sits on the payload attach fitting, on a Star 48-class solid motor, on the spin table that spins it up before it fires.
pros: The kick motor adds two tonnes of propellant
Spin-stabilised: no guidance needed for the burn
cons: Solid motor: low Isp, one burn
No escape tower
Tall nose: needs engine steering (a gimbal ring) or bigger fins
